correctness.rationale: A disconnected five-vertex graph has at most three unordered disjoint present-edge pairs; equality classifies precisely the 15 component-clique graphs of types 4+1 and 3+2. Matching independence gives 15p^2<=3. Equality forces exact edge marginals and support; matched-pair probabilities and four-point equations yield one unique positive probability vector, explicitly (sqrt5-2)/5 on five isolates and (3-sqrt5)/10 on ten 3+2 splits. Substitution verifies matching independence, and a complete induced-triple versus complementary-edge calculation verifies full subgraph independence. Exact standalone code independently enumerated all 1024 finite graphs and checked every induced-state joint law.

value.rationale: This is a complete, naturally motivated equality-case classification at the first nontrivial five-vertex instance of the published dependence hierarchy. It shows that relaxing full induced-subgraph independence to matching independence cannot create additional extremal disconnected laws at the critical edge density. The exact rigidity determines all nonsymmetric probability measures and informs separation problems for larger n rather than furnishing a routine numerical bound.
